scenes.setting: Northampton. A Room of State in the Palace.

lines.text: Enter King John, Queen Eleanor, Pembroke, Essex, Salisbury and others with Chatillion.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Now, say, Chatillion, what would France with us?

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Thus, after greeting, speaks the King of France

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: In my behaviour to the majesty,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: The borrow’d majesty, of England here.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: A strange beginning: “borrow’d majesty”!

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Silence, good mother; hear the embassy.

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Philip of France, in right and true behalf

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Of thy deceased brother Geoffrey’s son,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Arthur Plantagenet, lays most lawful claim

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: To this fair island and the territories,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: To Ireland, Poitiers, Anjou, Touraine, Maine,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Desiring thee to lay aside the sword

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Which sways usurpingly these several titles,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: And put the same into young Arthur’s hand,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Thy nephew and right royal sovereign.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: What follows if we disallow of this?

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: The proud control of fierce and bloody war,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: To enforce these rights so forcibly withheld.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Here have we war for war and blood for blood,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Controlment for controlment: so answer France.

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: Then take my king’s defiance from my mouth,

lines.speaker: CHATILLION
lines.text: The farthest limit of my embassy.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Bear mine to him, and so depart in peace.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Be thou as lightning in the eyes of France,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: For ere thou canst report, I will be there,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: The thunder of my cannon shall be heard.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: So, hence! Be thou the trumpet of our wrath

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And sullen presage of your own decay.—

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: An honourable conduct let him have.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Pembroke, look to ’t. Farewell, Chatillion.
[_Exeunt Chatillion and Pembroke._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: What now, my son! Have I not ever said

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: How that ambitious Constance would not cease

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Till she had kindled France and all the world

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Upon the right and party of her son?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: This might have been prevented and made whole

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: With very easy arguments of love,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Which now the manage of two kingdoms must

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: With fearful bloody issue arbitrate.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Our strong possession and our right for us.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Your strong possession much more than your right,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Or else it must go wrong with you and me:

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: So much my conscience whispers in your ear,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Which none but heaven and you and I shall hear.
Enter a Sheriff, who whispers to Essex.

lines.speaker: ESSEX
lines.text: My liege, here is the strangest controversy,

lines.speaker: ESSEX
lines.text: Come from the country to be judg’d by you,

lines.speaker: ESSEX
lines.text: That e’er I heard. Shall I produce the men?

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Let them approach.
[_Exit Sheriff._]

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Our abbeys and our priories shall pay

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: This expedition’s charge.
Enter Robert Faulconbridge and Philip, his Bastard brother.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: What men are you?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Your faithful subject I, a gentleman

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Born in Northamptonshire, and eldest son,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: As I suppose, to Robert Faulconbridge,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: A soldier by the honour-giving hand

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Of Cœur-de-lion knighted in the field.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: What art thou?

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: The son and heir to that same Faulconbridge.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Is that the elder, and art thou the heir?

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: You came not of one mother then, it seems.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Most certain of one mother, mighty king;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: That is well known; and, as I think, one father.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But for the certain knowledge of that truth

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I put you o’er to heaven and to my mother.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Of that I doubt, as all men’s children may.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Out on thee, rude man! Thou dost shame thy mother

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: And wound her honour with this diffidence.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I, madam? No, I have no reason for it;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: That is my brother’s plea, and none of mine;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: The which if he can prove, he pops me out

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: At least from fair five hundred pound a year.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Heaven guard my mother’s honour and my land!

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: A good blunt fellow. Why, being younger born,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Doth he lay claim to thine inheritance?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I know not why, except to get the land.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But once he slander’d me with bastardy.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But whe’er I be as true begot or no,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: That still I lay upon my mother’s head;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But that I am as well begot, my liege—

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Fair fall the bones that took the pains for me!—

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Compare our faces and be judge yourself.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: If old Sir Robert did beget us both

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And were our father, and this son like him,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: O old Sir Robert, father, on my knee

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I give heaven thanks I was not like to thee!

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Why, what a madcap hath heaven lent us here!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: He hath a trick of Cœur-de-lion’s face;

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: The accent of his tongue affecteth him.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Do you not read some tokens of my son

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: In the large composition of this man?

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Mine eye hath well examined his parts

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And finds them perfect Richard. Sirrah, speak,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: What doth move you to claim your brother’s land?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Because he hath a half-face, like my father.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: With half that face would he have all my land:

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: A half-fac’d groat five hundred pound a year!

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: My gracious liege, when that my father liv’d,

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Your brother did employ my father much—

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Well, sir, by this you cannot get my land.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Your tale must be how he employ’d my mother.

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: And once dispatch’d him in an embassy

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: To Germany, there with the emperor

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: To treat of high affairs touching that time.

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Th’ advantage of his absence took the King

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: And in the meantime sojourn’d at my father’s;

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Where how he did prevail I shame to speak;

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: But truth is truth: large lengths of seas and shores

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Between my father and my mother lay,

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: As I have heard my father speak himself,

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: When this same lusty gentleman was got.

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Upon his death-bed he by will bequeath’d

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: His lands to me, and took it, on his death

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: That this my mother’s son was none of his;

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: And if he were, he came into the world

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Full fourteen weeks before the course of time.

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Then, good my liege, let me have what is mine,

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: My father’s land, as was my father’s will.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Sirrah, your brother is legitimate;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Your father’s wife did after wedlock bear him,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And if she did play false, the fault was hers;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Which fault lies on the hazards of all husbands

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: That marry wives. Tell me, how if my brother,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Who, as you say, took pains to get this son,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Had of your father claim’d this son for his?

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: In sooth, good friend, your father might have kept

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: This calf, bred from his cow, from all the world;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: In sooth, he might; then, if he were my brother’s,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: My brother might not claim him; nor your father,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Being none of his, refuse him. This concludes;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: My mother’s son did get your father’s heir;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Your father’s heir must have your father’s land.

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: Shall then my father’s will be of no force

lines.speaker: ROBERT
lines.text: To dispossess that child which is not his?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Of no more force to dispossess me, sir,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Than was his will to get me, as I think.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Whether hadst thou rather be: a Faulconbridge

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: And like thy brother, to enjoy thy land,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Or the reputed son of Cœur-de-lion,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Lord of thy presence and no land besides?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Madam, and if my brother had my shape

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And I had his, Sir Robert’s his, like him;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And if my legs were two such riding-rods,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: My arms such eel-skins stuff’d, my face so thin

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: That in mine ear I durst not stick a rose

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Lest men should say “Look where three-farthings goes!”

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And, to his shape, were heir to all this land,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Would I might never stir from off this place,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I would give it every foot to have this face.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I would not be Sir Nob in any case.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: I like thee well. Wilt thou forsake thy fortune,

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Bequeath thy land to him, and follow me?

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: I am a soldier and now bound to France.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Brother, take you my land, I’ll take my chance.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Your face hath got five hundred pound a year,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Yet sell your face for five pence and ’tis dear.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Madam, I’ll follow you unto the death.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Nay, I would have you go before me thither.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Our country manners give our betters way.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: What is thy name?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Philip, my liege, so is my name begun;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Philip, good old Sir Robert’s wife’s eldest son.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: From henceforth bear his name whose form thou bearest.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Kneel thou down Philip, but rise more great,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Arise Sir Richard and Plantagenet.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Brother by th’ mother’s side, give me your hand.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: My father gave me honour, yours gave land.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Now blessed be the hour, by night or day,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: When I was got, Sir Robert was away!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: The very spirit of Plantagenet!

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: I am thy grandam, Richard; call me so.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Madam, by chance but not by truth; what though?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Something about, a little from the right,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: In at the window, or else o’er the hatch.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Who dares not stir by day must walk by night,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And have is have, however men do catch.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Near or far off, well won is still well shot,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And I am I, howe’er I was begot.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Go, Faulconbridge; now hast thou thy desire.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: A landless knight makes thee a landed squire.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Come, madam, and come, Richard, we must speed

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: For France, for France, for it is more than need.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Brother, adieu, good fortune come to thee!

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: For thou wast got i’ th’ way of honesty.
[_Exeunt all but the Bastard._]

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: A foot of honour better than I was,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But many a many foot of land the worse.

lines.text: Well, now can I make any Joan a lady.

lines.speaker: BASTARD

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And if his name be George, I’ll call him Peter;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: For new-made honour doth forget men’s names:

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: ’Tis too respective and too sociable

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: For your conversion. Now your traveller,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: He and his toothpick at my worship’s mess,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And when my knightly stomach is suffic’d,

lines.text: Why then I suck my teeth and catechize

lines.text: My picked man of countries: “My dear sir,”

lines.text: Thus leaning on mine elbow I begin,

lines.text: “I shall beseech you”—that is Question now;

lines.text: And then comes Answer like an absey book:

lines.text: “O sir,” says Answer “at your best command;

lines.text: At your employment; at your service, sir.”

lines.text: “No, sir,” says Question, “I, sweet sir, at yours.”

lines.text: And so, ere Answer knows what Question would,

lines.text: For he is but a bastard to the time

lines.text: That doth not smack of observation,

lines.text: And so am I, whether I smack or no;

lines.text: And not alone in habit and device,

lines.text: Exterior form, outward accoutrement,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But from the inward motion to deliver

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Sweet, sweet, sweet poison for the age’s tooth,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Which, though I will not practise to deceive,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Yet, to avoid deceit, I mean to learn;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: For it shall strew the footsteps of my rising.

lines.text: But who comes in such haste in riding-robes?

lines.text: What woman-post is this? Hath she no husband

lines.text: Madam, I was not old Sir Robert’s son.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Makes it take head from all indifferency,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: From all direction, purpose, course, intent.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And this same bias, this commodity,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: This bawd, this broker, this all-changing word,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Clapp’d on the outward eye of fickle France,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Hath drawn him from his own determin’d aid,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: From a resolv’d and honourable war,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: To a most base and vile-concluded peace.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And why rail I on this commodity?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But for because he hath not woo’d me yet.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Not that I have the power to clutch my hand

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: When his fair angels would salute my palm;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But for my hand, as unattempted yet,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Like a poor beggar, raileth on the rich.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Well, whiles I am a beggar, I will rail

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And say there is no sin but to be rich;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And being rich, my virtue then shall be

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: To say there is no vice but beggary.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Since kings break faith upon commodity,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Gain, be my lord, for I will worship thee!
[_Exit._]
Enter Constance, Arthur and Salisbury.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Gone to be married? Gone to swear a peace?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: False blood to false blood join’d? Gone to be friends?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Shall Louis have Blanche, and Blanche those provinces?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: It is not so; thou hast misspoke, misheard;

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Be well advis’d, tell o’er thy tale again.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: It cannot be; thou dost but say ’tis so.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: I trust I may not trust thee, for thy word

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Is but the vain breath of a common man.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Believe me, I do not believe thee, man.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: I have a king’s oath to the contrary.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Thou shalt be punish’d for thus frighting me,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: For I am sick and capable of fears,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Oppress’d with wrongs, and therefore full of fears,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: A widow, husbandless, subject to fears,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: A woman, naturally born to fears,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And though thou now confess thou didst but jest,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: With my vex’d spirits I cannot take a truce,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: But they will quake and tremble all this day.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: What dost thou mean by shaking of thy head?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Why dost thou look so sadly on my son?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: What means that hand upon that breast of thine?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Why holds thine eye that lamentable rheum,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Like a proud river peering o’er his bounds?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Be these sad signs confirmers of thy words?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Then speak again—not all thy former tale,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: But this one word, whether thy tale be true.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: As true as I believe you think them false

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: That give you cause to prove my saying true.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: O, if thou teach me to believe this sorrow,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Teach thou this sorrow how to make me die,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And let belief and life encounter so

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: As doth the fury of two desperate men

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Which in the very meeting fall and die.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Louis marry Blanche? O boy, then where art thou?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: France friend with England? What becomes of me?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Fellow, be gone. I cannot brook thy sight.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: This news hath made thee a most ugly man.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: What other harm have I, good lady, done,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: But spoke the harm that is by others done?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Which harm within itself so heinous is,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: As it makes harmful all that speak of it.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I do beseech you, madam, be content.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: If thou, that bid’st me be content, wert grim,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Ugly, and sland’rous to thy mother’s womb,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Full of unpleasing blots and sightless stains,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Lame, foolish, crooked, swart, prodigious,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Patch’d with foul moles and eye-offending marks,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: I would not care, I then would be content,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: For then I should not love thee; no, nor thou

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Become thy great birth, nor deserve a crown.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: But thou art fair, and at thy birth, dear boy,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Nature and Fortune join’d to make thee great.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Of Nature’s gifts thou mayst with lilies boast,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And with the half-blown rose. But Fortune, O,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: She is corrupted, chang’d, and won from thee;

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: She adulterates hourly with thine uncle John,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And with her golden hand hath pluck’d on France

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: To tread down fair respect of sovereignty,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And made his majesty the bawd to theirs.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: France is a bawd to Fortune and King John,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: That strumpet Fortune, that usurping John!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Tell me, thou fellow, is not France forsworn?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Envenom him with words, or get thee gone,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And leave those woes alone which I alone

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Am bound to underbear.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Pardon me, madam,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: I may not go without you to the Kings.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Thou mayst, thou shalt; I will not go with thee.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: I will instruct my sorrows to be proud,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: For grief is proud and makes his owner stoop.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: To me and to the state of my great grief

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Let kings assemble; for my grief’s so great

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: That no supporter but the huge firm earth

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Can hold it up. Here I and sorrows sit;

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Here is my throne, bid kings come bow to it.
[_Seats herself on the ground._]
Enter King John, King Philip, Louis, Blanche, Eleanor, Bastard, Austria and attendants.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: ’Tis true, fair daughter; and this blessed day

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Ever in France shall be kept festival.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: To solemnize this day the glorious sun

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Stays in his course and plays the alchemist,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Turning with splendour of his precious eye

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: The meagre cloddy earth to glittering gold.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: The yearly course that brings this day about

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Shall never see it but a holy day.
[_Rising_.]

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: A wicked day, and not a holy day!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: What hath this day deserv’d? What hath it done

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: That it in golden letters should be set

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Among the high tides in the calendar?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Nay, rather turn this day out of the week,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: This day of shame, oppression, perjury.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Or, if it must stand still, let wives with child

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Pray that their burdens may not fall this day,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Lest that their hopes prodigiously be cross’d.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: But on this day let seamen fear no wrack;

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: No bargains break that are not this day made;

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: This day, all things begun come to ill end,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Yea, faith itself to hollow falsehood change!

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: By heaven, lady, you shall have no cause

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: To curse the fair proceedings of this day.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Have I not pawn’d to you my majesty?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: You have beguil’d me with a counterfeit

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Resembling majesty, which, being touch’d and tried,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Proves valueless. You are forsworn, forsworn.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: You came in arms to spill mine enemies’ blood,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: But now in arms you strengthen it with yours.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: The grappling vigour and rough frown of war

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Is cold in amity and painted peace,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And our oppression hath made up this league.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Arm, arm, you heavens, against these perjur’d kings!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: A widow cries; be husband to me, heavens!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Let not the hours of this ungodly day

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Wear out the day in peace; but, ere sunset,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Set armed discord ’twixt these perjur’d kings!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Hear me, O, hear me!

lines.speaker: AUSTRIA
lines.text: Lady Constance, peace!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: War! war! no peace! Peace is to me a war.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: O Limoges, O Austria, thou dost shame

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: That bloody spoil. Thou slave, thou wretch, thou coward!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Thou little valiant, great in villainy!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Thou ever strong upon the stronger side!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Thou Fortune’s champion that dost never fight

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: But when her humorous ladyship is by

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: To teach thee safety! Thou art perjur’d too,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And sooth’st up greatness. What a fool art thou,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: A ramping fool, to brag, and stamp, and swear

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Upon my party! Thou cold-blooded slave,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Hast thou not spoke like thunder on my side?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Been sworn my soldier, bidding me depend

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Upon thy stars, thy fortune, and thy strength?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And dost thou now fall over to my foes?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Thou wear a lion’s hide! Doff it for shame,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And hang a calf’s-skin on those recreant limbs.

lines.speaker: AUSTRIA
lines.text: O that a man should speak those words to me!

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And hang a calf’s-skin on those recreant limbs.

lines.speaker: AUSTRIA
lines.text: Thou dar’st not say so, villain, for thy life.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And hang a calf’s-skin on those recreant limbs.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: We like not this. Thou dost forget thyself.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Here comes the holy legate of the Pope.
Enter Pandulph.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Hail, you anointed deputies of heaven!

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: To thee, King John, my holy errand is.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: I Pandulph, of fair Milan cardinal,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And from Pope Innocent the legate here,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Do in his name religiously demand

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Why thou against the church, our holy mother,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: So wilfully dost spurn; and force perforce

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Keep Stephen Langton, chosen Archbishop

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Of Canterbury, from that holy see.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: This, in our foresaid holy father’s name,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Pope Innocent, I do demand of thee.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: What earthy name to interrogatories

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Can task the free breath of a sacred king?

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Thou canst not, cardinal, devise a name

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: So slight, unworthy, and ridiculous,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: To charge me to an answer, as the pope.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Tell him this tale; and from the mouth of England

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Add thus much more, that no Italian priest

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Shall tithe or toll in our dominions;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: But as we under God are supreme head,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: So, under Him, that great supremacy,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Where we do reign, we will alone uphold

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Without th’ assistance of a mortal hand.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: So tell the pope, all reverence set apart

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: To him and his usurp’d authority.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Brother of England, you blaspheme in this.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Though you and all the kings of Christendom

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Are led so grossly by this meddling priest,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Dreading the curse that money may buy out;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And by the merit of vile gold, dross, dust,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Purchase corrupted pardon of a man,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Who in that sale sells pardon from himself;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Though you and all the rest, so grossly led,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: This juggling witchcraft with revenue cherish,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Yet I alone, alone do me oppose

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Against the pope, and count his friends my foes.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Then, by the lawful power that I have,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Thou shalt stand curs’d and excommunicate;

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And blessed shall he be that doth revolt

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: From his allegiance to an heretic;

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And meritorious shall that hand be call’d,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Canonized and worshipp’d as a saint,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: That takes away by any secret course

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Thy hateful life.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: O, lawful let it be

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: That I have room with Rome to curse awhile!

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Good father Cardinal, cry thou amen

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: To my keen curses; for without my wrong

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: There is no tongue hath power to curse him right.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: There’s law and warrant, lady, for my curse.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And for mine too. When law can do no right,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Let it be lawful that law bar no wrong.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Law cannot give my child his kingdom here,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: For he that holds his kingdom holds the law;

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Therefore, since law itself is perfect wrong,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: How can the law forbid my tongue to curse?

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Philip of France, on peril of a curse,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Let go the hand of that arch-heretic,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And raise the power of France upon his head,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Unless he do submit himself to Rome.

lines.speaker: QUEEN ELEANOR
lines.text: Look’st thou pale, France? Do not let go thy hand.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Look to that, devil, lest that France repent

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: And by disjoining hands, hell lose a soul.

lines.speaker: AUSTRIA
lines.text: King Philip, listen to the cardinal.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And hang a calf’s-skin on his recreant limbs.

lines.speaker: AUSTRIA
lines.text: Well, ruffian, I must pocket up these wrongs,

lines.speaker: AUSTRIA
lines.text: Because—

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Your breeches best may carry them.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Philip, what say’st thou to the cardinal?

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: What should he say, but as the cardinal?

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Bethink you, father; for the difference

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Is purchase of a heavy curse from Rome,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Or the light loss of England for a friend.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Forgo the easier.

lines.speaker: BLANCHE
lines.text: That’s the curse of Rome.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: O Louis, stand fast! The devil tempts thee here

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: In likeness of a new untrimmed bride.

lines.speaker: BLANCHE
lines.text: The Lady Constance speaks not from her faith,

lines.speaker: BLANCHE
lines.text: But from her need.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: O, if thou grant my need,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Which only lives but by the death of faith,

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: That need must needs infer this principle:

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: That faith would live again by death of need.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: O then tread down my need, and faith mounts up;

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: Keep my need up, and faith is trodden down!

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: The King is mov’d, and answers not to this.

lines.speaker: CONSTANCE
lines.text: O, be remov’d from him, and answer well!

lines.speaker: AUSTRIA
lines.text: Do so, King Philip; hang no more in doubt.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Hang nothing but a calf’s-skin, most sweet lout.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: I am perplex’d, and know not what to say.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: What canst thou say but will perplex thee more,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: If thou stand excommunicate and curs’d?

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Good reverend father, make my person yours,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: And tell me how you would bestow yourself.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: This royal hand and mine are newly knit,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: And the conjunction of our inward souls

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Married in league, coupled and link’d together

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: With all religious strength of sacred vows;

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: The latest breath that gave the sound of words

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Was deep-sworn faith, peace, amity, true love

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Between our kingdoms and our royal selves;

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: And even before this truce, but new before,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: No longer than we well could wash our hands

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: To clap this royal bargain up of peace,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Heaven knows, they were besmear’d and overstain’d

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: With slaughter’s pencil, where revenge did paint

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: The fearful difference of incensed kings.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: And shall these hands, so lately purg’d of blood,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: So newly join’d in love, so strong in both,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Unyoke this seizure and this kind regreet?

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Play fast and loose with faith? So jest with heaven,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Make such unconstant children of ourselves,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: As now again to snatch our palm from palm,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Unswear faith sworn, and on the marriage-bed

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Of smiling peace to march a bloody host,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: And make a riot on the gentle brow

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Of true sincerity? O, holy sir,

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: My reverend father, let it not be so!

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Out of your grace, devise, ordain, impose

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: Some gentle order, and then we shall be blest

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: To do your pleasure and continue friends.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: All form is formless, order orderless,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Save what is opposite to England’s love.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Therefore to arms! Be champion of our church,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Or let the church, our mother, breathe her curse,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: A mother’s curse, on her revolting son.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: France, thou mayst hold a serpent by the tongue,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: A chafed lion by the mortal paw,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: A fasting tiger safer by the tooth,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Than keep in peace that hand which thou dost hold.

lines.speaker: KING PHILIP
lines.text: I may disjoin my hand, but not my faith.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: So mak’st thou faith an enemy to faith,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And like a civil war sett’st oath to oath,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Thy tongue against thy tongue. O, let thy vow

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: First made to heaven, first be to heaven perform’d,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: That is, to be the champion of our church.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: What since thou swor’st is sworn against thyself

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And may not be performed by thyself,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: For that which thou hast sworn to do amiss

lines.speaker: PANDULPH

lines.text: In this which he accounts so clearly won.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Are not you griev’d that Arthur is his prisoner?

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: As heartily as he is glad he hath him.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Your mind is all as youthful as your blood.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Now hear me speak with a prophetic spirit;

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: For even the breath of what I mean to speak

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Shall blow each dust, each straw, each little rub,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Out of the path which shall directly lead

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Thy foot to England’s throne; and therefore mark.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: John hath seiz’d Arthur; and it cannot be

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: That, whiles warm life plays in that infant’s veins,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: The misplac’d John should entertain an hour,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: One minute, nay, one quiet breath of rest.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: A sceptre snatch’d with an unruly hand

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Must be boisterously maintain’d as gain’d.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And he that stands upon a slipp’ry place

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Makes nice of no vile hold to stay him up.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: That John may stand, then, Arthur needs must fall.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: So be it, for it cannot be but so.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: But what shall I gain by young Arthur’s fall?

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: You, in the right of Lady Blanche your wife,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: May then make all the claim that Arthur did.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: And lose it, life and all, as Arthur did.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: How green you are and fresh in this old world!

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: John lays you plots; the times conspire with you;

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: For he that steeps his safety in true blood

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Shall find but bloody safety and untrue.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: This act so evilly borne shall cool the hearts

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Of all his people, and freeze up their zeal,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: That none so small advantage shall step forth

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: To check his reign, but they will cherish it;

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: No natural exhalation in the sky,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: No scope of nature, no distemper’d day,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: No common wind, no customed event,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: But they will pluck away his natural cause

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And call them meteors, prodigies, and signs,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Abortives, presages, and tongues of heaven,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Plainly denouncing vengeance upon John.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Maybe he will not touch young Arthur’s life,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: But hold himself safe in his prisonment.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: O, sir, when he shall hear of your approach,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: If that young Arthur be not gone already,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Even at that news he dies; and then the hearts

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Of all his people shall revolt from him,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And kiss the lips of unacquainted change,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And pick strong matter of revolt and wrath

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Out of the bloody fingers’ ends of John.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Methinks I see this hurly all on foot;

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: And, O, what better matter breeds for you

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Than I have nam’d! The bastard Faulconbridge

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Is now in England ransacking the church,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Offending charity. If but a dozen French

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Were there in arms, they would be as a call

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: To train ten thousand English to their side,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Or as a little snow, tumbled about,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Anon becomes a mountain. O noble Dauphin,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Go with me to the King. ’Tis wonderful

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: What may be wrought out of their discontent,

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: Now that their souls are topful of offence.

lines.speaker: PANDULPH
lines.text: For England go. I will whet on the King.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Strong reasons makes strong actions. Let us go.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: If you say ay, the King will not say no.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Northampton. A Room in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Hubert and two Executioners.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Heat me these irons hot; and look thou stand

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Within the arras. When I strike my foot

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Upon the bosom of the ground, rush forth

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: And bind the boy which you shall find with me

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Fast to the chair. Be heedful. Hence, and watch.

lines.speaker: FIRST EXECUTIONER
lines.text: I hope your warrant will bear out the deed.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Uncleanly scruples! Fear not you; look to’t.
[_Exeunt Executioners._]

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Young lad, come forth; I have to say with you.
Enter Arthur.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Good morrow, Hubert.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Good morrow, little prince.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: As little prince, having so great a title

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: To be more prince, as may be. You are sad.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Indeed, I have been merrier.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Mercy on me!

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Methinks nobody should be sad but I.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Yet, I remember, when I was in France,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Young gentlemen would be as sad as night,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Only for wantonness. By my christendom,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: So I were out of prison, and kept sheep,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I should be as merry as the day is long;

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And so I would be here, but that I doubt

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: My uncle practises more harm to me.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: He is afraid of me, and I of him.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Is it my fault that I was Geoffrey’s son?

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: No, indeed, is’t not; and I would to heaven

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I were your son, so you would love me, Hubert.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: If I talk to him, with his innocent prate

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: He will awake my mercy, which lies dead.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Therefore I will be sudden and dispatch.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Are you sick, Hubert? You look pale today.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: In sooth, I would you were a little sick,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: That I might sit all night and watch with you.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I warrant I love you more than you do me.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: His words do take possession of my bosom.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Read here, young Arthur.
[_Showing a paper._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: How now, foolish rheum!

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Turning dispiteous torture out of door!

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: I must be brief, lest resolution drop

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Out at mine eyes in tender womanish tears.—

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Can you not read it? Is it not fair writ?

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Too fairly, Hubert, for so foul effect.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Must you with hot irons burn out both mine eyes?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Young boy, I must.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And will you?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: And I will.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Have you the heart? When your head did but ache,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I knit my handkercher about your brows,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: The best I had, a princess wrought it me,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And I did never ask it you again;

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And with my hand at midnight held your head,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And, like the watchful minutes to the hour,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Still and anon cheer’d up the heavy time,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Saying ’What lack you?” and “Where lies your grief?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Or “What good love may I perform for you?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Many a poor man’s son would have lien still

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And ne’er have spoke a loving word to you;

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: But you at your sick service had a prince.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Nay, you may think my love was crafty love,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And call it cunning. Do, an if you will.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: If heaven be pleas’d that you must use me ill,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Why then you must. Will you put out mine eyes?

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: These eyes that never did nor never shall

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: So much as frown on you?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: I have sworn to do it.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: And with hot irons must I burn them out.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Ah, none but in this iron age would do it!

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: The iron of itself, though heat red-hot,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Approaching near these eyes would drink my tears

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And quench his fiery indignation

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Even in the matter of mine innocence;

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Nay, after that, consume away in rust,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: But for containing fire to harm mine eye.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Are you more stubborn-hard than hammer’d iron?

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: An if an angel should have come to me

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And told me Hubert should put out mine eyes,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I would not have believ’d him. No tongue but Hubert’s.
[_Stamps_.]

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Come forth.
Enter Executioners with cords, irons, &c.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Do as I bid you do.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: O, save me, Hubert, save me! My eyes are out

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Even with the fierce looks of these bloody men.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Give me the iron, I say, and bind him here.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Alas, what need you be so boist’rous-rough?

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I will not struggle, I will stand stone-still.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: For heaven sake, Hubert, let me not be bound!

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Nay, hear me, Hubert! Drive these men away,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And I will sit as quiet as a lamb;

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: I will not stir, nor wince, nor speak a word,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Nor look upon the iron angerly.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Thrust but these men away, and I’ll forgive you,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Whatever torment you do put me to.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Go, stand within; let me alone with him.

lines.speaker: FIRST EXECUTIONER
lines.text: I am best pleas’d to be from such a deed.
[_Exeunt Executioners._]

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Alas, I then have chid away my friend!

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: He hath a stern look but a gentle heart.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Let him come back, that his compassion may

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Give life to yours.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Come, boy, prepare yourself.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Is there no remedy?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: None, but to lose your eyes.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: O heaven, that there were but a mote in yours,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: A grain, a dust, a gnat, a wandering hair,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Any annoyance in that precious sense!

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Then, feeling what small things are boisterous there,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Your vile intent must needs seem horrible.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Is this your promise? Go to, hold your tongue.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Hubert, the utterance of a brace of tongues

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Must needs want pleading for a pair of eyes.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Let me not hold my tongue. Let me not, Hubert,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Or, Hubert, if you will, cut out my tongue,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: So I may keep mine eyes. O, spare mine eyes,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Though to no use but still to look on you!

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Lo, by my troth, the instrument is cold

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And would not harm me.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: I can heat it, boy.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: No, in good sooth; the fire is dead with grief,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Being create for comfort, to be us’d

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: In undeserv’d extremes. See else yourself.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: There is no malice in this burning coal;

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: The breath of heaven hath blown his spirit out

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And strew’d repentant ashes on his head.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: But with my breath I can revive it, boy.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: An if you do, you will but make it blush

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And glow with shame of your proceedings, Hubert.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Nay, it perchance will sparkle in your eyes;

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: And, like a dog that is compell’d to fight,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Snatch at his master that doth tarre him on.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: All things that you should use to do me wrong

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Deny their office. Only you do lack

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: That mercy which fierce fire and iron extends,

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: Creatures of note for mercy-lacking uses.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Well, see to live; I will not touch thine eye

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: For all the treasure that thine uncle owes.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Yet I am sworn, and I did purpose, boy,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: With this same very iron to burn them out.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: O, now you look like Hubert! All this while

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: You were disguised.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Peace; no more. Adieu.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Your uncle must not know but you are dead.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: I’ll fill these dogged spies with false reports.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: And, pretty child, sleep doubtless and secure

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: That Hubert, for the wealth of all the world,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Will not offend thee.

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: O heaven! I thank you, Hubert.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Silence; no more. Go closely in with me.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Much danger do I undergo for thee.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A Room of State in the Palace.

lines.text: Enter King John, crowned, Pembroke, Salisbury and other Lords. The King takes his State.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Here once again we sit, once again crown’d,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And look’d upon, I hope, with cheerful eyes.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: This “once again,” but that your highness pleas’d,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Was once superfluous. You were crown’d before,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: And that high royalty was ne’er pluck’d off,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: The faiths of men ne’er stained with revolt;

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Fresh expectation troubled not the land

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: With any long’d-for change or better state.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Therefore, to be possess’d with double pomp,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To guard a title that was rich before,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To gild refined gold, to paint the lily,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To throw a perfume on the violet,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To smooth the ice, or add another hue

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Unto the rainbow, or with taper-light

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To seek the beauteous eye of heaven to garnish,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Is wasteful and ridiculous excess.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: But that your royal pleasure must be done,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: This act is as an ancient tale new told,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: And, in the last repeating, troublesome,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Being urged at a time unseasonable.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: In this the antique and well-noted face

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Of plain old form is much disfigured;

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And, like a shifted wind unto a sail,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: It makes the course of thoughts to fetch about,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Startles and frights consideration,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Makes sound opinion sick and truth suspected,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: For putting on so new a fashion’d robe.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: When workmen strive to do better than well,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: They do confound their skill in covetousness;

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: And oftentimes excusing of a fault

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Doth make the fault the worse by the excuse,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: As patches set upon a little breach

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Discredit more in hiding of the fault

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Than did the fault before it was so patch’d.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To this effect, before you were new-crown’d,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: We breath’d our counsel; but it pleas’d your highness

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To overbear it, and we are all well pleas’d,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Since all and every part of what we would

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Doth make a stand at what your highness will.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Some reasons of this double coronation

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: I have possess’d you with, and think them strong;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And more, more strong, when lesser is my fear,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: I shall indue you with. Meantime but ask

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: What you would have reform’d that is not well,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And well shall you perceive how willingly

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: I will both hear and grant you your requests.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Then I, as one that am the tongue of these,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: To sound the purposes of all their hearts,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Both for myself and them, but, chief of all,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Your safety, for the which myself and them

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Bend their best studies, heartily request

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Th’ enfranchisement of Arthur, whose restraint

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Doth move the murmuring lips of discontent

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: To break into this dangerous argument:

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: If what in rest you have in right you hold,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Why then your fears, which, as they say, attend

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: The steps of wrong, should move you to mew up

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Your tender kinsman, and to choke his days

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: With barbarous ignorance, and deny his youth

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: The rich advantage of good exercise?

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: That the time’s enemies may not have this

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: To grace occasions, let it be our suit

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: That you have bid us ask his liberty;

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Which for our goods we do no further ask

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Than whereupon our weal, on you depending,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Counts it your weal he have his liberty.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Let it be so. I do commit his youth

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: To your direction.
Enter Hubert.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Hubert, what news with you?
[_Taking him apart._]

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: This is the man should do the bloody deed.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: He show’d his warrant to a friend of mine.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: The image of a wicked heinous fault

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Lives in his eye; that close aspect of his

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Doth show the mood of a much troubled breast;

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: And I do fearfully believe ’tis done

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: What we so fear’d he had a charge to do.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: The colour of the King doth come and go

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Between his purpose and his conscience,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Like heralds ’twixt two dreadful battles set.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: His passion is so ripe it needs must break.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: And when it breaks, I fear will issue thence

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: The foul corruption of a sweet child’s death.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: We cannot hold mortality’s strong hand.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Good lords, although my will to give is living,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: The suit which you demand is gone and dead.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: He tells us Arthur is deceas’d tonight.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Indeed, we fear’d his sickness was past cure.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Indeed, we heard how near his death he was,

lines.text: And he that speaks doth gripe the hearer’s wrist,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: The whilst his iron did on the anvil cool,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Why seek’st thou to possess me with these fears?

lines.text: No had, my lord! Why, did you not provoke me?

lines.text: It is the curse of kings to be attended

lines.text: By slaves that take their humours for a warrant

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: To break within the bloody house of life,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And, on the winking of authority

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: To understand a law, to know the meaning

lines.speaker: KING JOHN

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: More upon humour than advis’d respect.

lines.text: Here is your hand and seal for what I did.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: O, when the last account ’twixt heaven and earth

lines.text: But taking note of thy abhorr’d aspect,

lines.text: Finding thee fit for bloody villainy,

lines.text: I faintly broke with thee of Arthur’s death;

lines.text: And thou, to be endeared to a king,

lines.text: When I spake darkly what I purpos’d,

lines.text: Or turn’d an eye of doubt upon my face,

lines.text: As bid me tell my tale in express words,

lines.text: Deep shame had struck me dumb, made me break off,

lines.text: But thou didst understand me by my signs

lines.text: And didst in signs again parley with sin;

lines.text: Between my conscience and my cousin’s death.

lines.text: Is yet a maiden and an innocent hand,

lines.text: Within this bosom never enter’d yet

lines.text: The dreadful motion of a murderous thought;

lines.text: And you have slander’d nature in my form,

lines.text: If that it be the work of any hand?

lines.text: It is the shameful work of Hubert’s hand,

lines.text: The practice and the purpose of the King,

lines.text: From whose obedience I forbid my soul,

lines.text: Kneeling before this ruin of sweet life,

lines.text: And breathing to his breathless excellence
