lines.text: Strike up the drums; and let the tongue of war,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Plead for our interest and our being here.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Indeed, your drums, being beaten, will cry out;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And so shall you, being beaten. Do but start

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And echo with the clamour of thy drum,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And even at hand a drum is ready brac’d

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: That shall reverberate all as loud as thine.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Sound but another, and another shall,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: As loud as thine, rattle the welkin’s ear

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And mock the deep-mouth’d thunder. For at hand,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Not trusting to this halting legate here,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Whom he hath us’d rather for sport than need,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Is warlike John; and in his forehead sits

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: A bare-ribb’d death, whose office is this day

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: To feast upon whole thousands of the French.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Strike up our drums, to find this danger out.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And thou shalt find it, Dauphin, do not doubt.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. The Field of Battle.

lines.text: Alarums. Enter King John and Hubert.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: How goes the day with us? O, tell me, Hubert.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Badly, I fear. How fares your majesty?

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: This fever that hath troubled me so long

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Lies heavy on me. O, my heart is sick!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: My lord, your valiant kinsman, Faulconbridge,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Desires your majesty to leave the field

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And send him word by me which way you go.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Tell him, toward Swinstead, to the abbey there.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Be of good comfort; for the great supply

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: That was expected by the Dauphin here

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Are wrack’d three nights ago on Goodwin Sands.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: This news was brought to Richard but even now.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The French fight coldly, and retire themselves.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Ay me, this tyrant fever burns me up

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And will not let me welcome this good news.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Set on toward Swinstead. To my litter straight.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Weakness possesseth me, and I am faint.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. Another part of the same.

lines.text: Enter Salisbury, Pembroke and Bigot.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: I did not think the King so stor’d with friends.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Up once again; put spirit in the French.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: If they miscarry, we miscarry too.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: That misbegotten devil, Faulconbridge,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: In spite of spite, alone upholds the day.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: They say King John, sore sick, hath left the field.
Enter Melun wounded, and led by Soldiers.

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Lead me to the revolts of England here.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: When we were happy we had other names.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: It is the Count Melun.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Wounded to death.

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Fly, noble English, you are bought and sold;

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Unthread the rude eye of rebellion

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: And welcome home again discarded faith.

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Seek out King John and fall before his feet;

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: For if the French be lords of this loud day,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: He means to recompense the pains you take

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: By cutting off your heads. Thus hath he sworn,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: And I with him, and many more with me,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Upon the altar at Saint Edmundsbury;

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Even on that altar where we swore to you

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Dear amity and everlasting love.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: May this be possible? May this be true?

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Have I not hideous death within my view,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Retaining but a quantity of life,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Which bleeds away even as a form of wax

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Resolveth from his figure ’gainst the fire?

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: What in the world should make me now deceive,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Since I must lose the use of all deceit?

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Why should I then be false, since it is true

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: That I must die here and live hence by truth?

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: I say again, if Louis do win the day,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: He is forsworn if e’er those eyes of yours

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Behold another day break in the east.

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: But even this night, whose black contagious breath

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Already smokes about the burning crest

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Of the old, feeble, and day-wearied sun,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Even this ill night, your breathing shall expire,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Paying the fine of rated treachery

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Even with a treacherous fine of all your lives,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: If Louis by your assistance win the day.

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Commend me to one Hubert, with your king;

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: The love of him, and this respect besides,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: For that my grandsire was an Englishman,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Awakes my conscience to confess all this.

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: In lieu whereof, I pray you, bear me hence

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: From forth the noise and rumour of the field,

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: Where I may think the remnant of my thoughts

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: In peace, and part this body and my soul

lines.speaker: MELUN
lines.text: With contemplation and devout desires.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: We do believe thee, and beshrew my soul

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: But I do love the favour and the form

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Of this most fair occasion, by the which

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: We will untread the steps of damned flight,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And like a bated and retired flood,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Leaving our rankness and irregular course,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Stoop low within those bounds we have o’erlook’d,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And calmly run on in obedience

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Even to our ocean, to our great King John.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: My arm shall give thee help to bear thee hence;

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: For I do see the cruel pangs of death

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Right in thine eye.—Away, my friends! New flight,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And happy newness, that intends old right.
[_Exeunt, leading off Melun._]
Enter Louis and his train.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: The sun of heaven, methought, was loath to set,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: But stay’d, and made the western welkin blush,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: When the English measure backward their own ground

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: In faint retire. O, bravely came we off,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: When with a volley of our needless shot,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: After such bloody toil, we bid good night,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: And wound our tott’ring colours clearly up,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Last in the field, and almost lords of it!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Where is my prince, the Dauphin?

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Here. What news?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The Count Melun is slain; the English lords

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: By his persuasion are again fall’n off,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: And your supply, which you have wish’d so long,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Are cast away and sunk on Goodwin Sands.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Ah, foul shrewd news! Beshrew thy very heart!

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: I did not think to be so sad tonight

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: As this hath made me. Who was he that said

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: King John did fly an hour or two before

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: The stumbling night did part our weary powers?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Whoever spoke it, it is true, my lord.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: Well, keep good quarter and good care tonight.

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: The day shall not be up so soon as I,

lines.speaker: LOUIS
lines.text: To try the fair adventure of tomorrow.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: An open place in the neighborhood of Swinstead Abbey.

lines.text: Enter the Bastard and Hubert, meeting.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Who’s there? Speak, ho! Speak quickly, or I shoot.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: A friend. What art thou?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Of the part of England.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Whither dost thou go?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: What’s that to thee? Why may I not demand

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Of thine affairs, as well as thou of mine?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Hubert, I think.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Thou hast a perfect thought.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: I will, upon all hazards, well believe

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Thou art my friend, that know’st my tongue so well.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Who art thou?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Who thou wilt. And if thou please,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Thou mayst befriend me so much as to think

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I come one way of the Plantagenets.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Unkind remembrance! Thou and eyeless night

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Have done me shame. Brave soldier, pardon me,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: That any accent breaking from thy tongue

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Should ’scape the true acquaintance of mine ear.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Come, come; sans compliment, what news abroad?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Why, here walk I in the black brow of night,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: To find you out.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Brief, then; and what’s the news?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: O, my sweet sir, news fitting to the night,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Black, fearful, comfortless, and horrible.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Show me the very wound of this ill news.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I am no woman, I’ll not swoon at it.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: The King, I fear, is poison’d by a monk.

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: I left him almost speechless, and broke out

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: To acquaint you with this evil, that you might

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: The better arm you to the sudden time,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Than if you had at leisure known of this.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: How did he take it? Who did taste to him?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: A monk, I tell you, a resolved villain,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Whose bowels suddenly burst out. The King

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Yet speaks, and peradventure may recover.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Who didst thou leave to tend his majesty?

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: Why, know you not? The lords are all come back,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: And brought Prince Henry in their company;

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: At whose request the King hath pardon’d them,

lines.speaker: HUBERT
lines.text: And they are all about his majesty.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Withhold thine indignation, mighty heaven,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And tempt us not to bear above our power!

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I’ll tell thee, Hubert, half my power this night,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Passing these flats, are taken by the tide;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: These Lincoln Washes have devoured them;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Myself, well mounted, hardly have escap’d.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Away, before. Conduct me to the King;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I doubt he will be dead or ere I come.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Prince Henry, Salisbury and Bigot.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: It is too late. The life of all his blood

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Is touch’d corruptibly, and his pure brain,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Which some suppose the soul’s frail dwelling-house,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Doth, by the idle comments that it makes,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Foretell the ending of mortality.
Enter Pembroke.

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: His Highness yet doth speak, and holds belief

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: That, being brought into the open air,

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: It would allay the burning quality

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Of that fell poison which assaileth him.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Let him be brought into the orchard here.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Doth he still rage?
[_Exit Bigot._]

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: He is more patient

lines.speaker: PEMBROKE
lines.text: Than when you left him; even now he sung.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: O vanity of sickness! Fierce extremes

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: In their continuance will not feel themselves.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Death, having prey’d upon the outward parts,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Leaves them invisible, and his siege is now

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Against the mind, the which he pricks and wounds

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: With many legions of strange fantasies,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Which, in their throng and press to that last hold,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Confound themselves. ’Tis strange that death should sing.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: I am the cygnet to this pale faint swan,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Who chants a doleful hymn to his own death

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: And from the organ-pipe of frailty sings

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: His soul and body to their lasting rest.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Be of good comfort, prince; for you are born

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To set a form upon that indigest

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Which he hath left so shapeless and so rude.
Enter Bigot and Attendants, who bring in King John in a chair.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Ay, marry, now my soul hath elbow-room

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: It would not out at windows nor at doors.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: There is so hot a summer in my bosom

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: That all my bowels crumble up to dust.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: I am a scribbled form, drawn with a pen

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Upon a parchment, and against this fire

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Do I shrink up.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: How fares your majesty?

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Poison’d, ill fare; dead, forsook, cast off,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And none of you will bid the winter come

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: To thrust his icy fingers in my maw,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Nor let my kingdom’s rivers take their course

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Through my burn’d bosom, nor entreat the north

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: To make his bleak winds kiss my parched lips

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And comfort me with cold. I do not ask you much,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: I beg cold comfort; and you are so strait,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And so ingrateful, you deny me that.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: O, that there were some virtue in my tears

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: That might relieve you!

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: The salt in them is hot.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Within me is a hell; and there the poison

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Is, as a fiend, confin’d to tyrannize

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: On unreprievable condemned blood.
Enter the Bastard.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: O, I am scalded with my violent motion

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And spleen of speed to see your majesty!

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: O cousin, thou art come to set mine eye.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: The tackle of my heart is crack’d and burn’d,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And all the shrouds wherewith my life should sail

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Are turned to one thread, one little hair.

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: My heart hath one poor string to stay it by,

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: Which holds but till thy news be uttered;

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And then all this thou seest is but a clod

lines.speaker: KING JOHN
lines.text: And module of confounded royalty.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: The Dauphin is preparing hitherward,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Where God He knows how we shall answer him;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: For in a night the best part of my power,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: As I upon advantage did remove,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Were in the Washes all unwarily

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Devoured by the unexpected flood.
[_The King dies._]

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: You breathe these dead news in as dead an ear.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: My liege! My lord!—But now a king, now thus.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: Even so must I run on, and even so stop.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: What surety of the world, what hope, what stay,

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: When this was now a king, and now is clay?

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Art thou gone so? I do but stay behind

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: To do the office for thee of revenge,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And then my soul shall wait on thee to heaven,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: As it on earth hath been thy servant still.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Now, now, you stars that move in your right spheres,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Where be your powers? Show now your mended faiths,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And instantly return with me again,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: To push destruction and perpetual shame

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Out of the weak door of our fainting land.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Straight let us seek, or straight we shall be sought;

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: The Dauphin rages at our very heels.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: It seems you know not, then, so much as we.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: The Cardinal Pandulph is within at rest,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Who half an hour since came from the Dauphin,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And brings from him such offers of our peace

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: As we with honour and respect may take,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: With purpose presently to leave this war.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: He will the rather do it when he sees

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Ourselves well sinewed to our defence.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Nay, ’tis in a manner done already,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: For many carriages he hath dispatch’d

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To the sea-side, and put his cause and quarrel

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To the disposing of the cardinal,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: With whom yourself, myself, and other lords,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: If you think meet, this afternoon will post

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To consummate this business happily.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Let it be so. And you, my noble prince,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: With other princes that may best be spar’d,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Shall wait upon your father’s funeral.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: At Worcester must his body be interr’d;

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: For so he will’d it.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Thither shall it, then,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And happily may your sweet self put on

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: The lineal state and glory of the land!

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: To whom, with all submission, on my knee,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: I do bequeath my faithful services

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And true subjection everlastingly.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And the like tender of our love we make,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: To rest without a spot for evermore.

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: I have a kind soul that would give you thanks

lines.speaker: PRINCE HENRY
lines.text: And knows not how to do it but with tears.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: O, let us pay the time but needful woe,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Since it hath been beforehand with our griefs.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: This England never did, nor never shall,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Lie at the proud foot of a conqueror,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: But when it first did help to wound itself.

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Now these her princes are come home again,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: Come the three corners of the world in arms

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: And we shall shock them. Nought shall make us rue,

lines.speaker: BASTARD
lines.text: If England to itself do rest but true.
[_Exeunt._]
